facts.text: Screenwriter Ed Naha said C.H.U.D. II started out as a planned sequel to Return of the Living Dead, not to the 1984 C.H.U.D. It got retooled into a C.H.U.D. follow-up.
Gerrit Graham, who plays Bud, later became a writer on VH1's Pop Up Video, the show this very bubble style is copying.
Robert Vaughn (Colonel Masters) had only 16 lines in The Magnificent Seven, and was convinced both it and Bullitt would be box-office poison.
Director David Irving shot three versions of the film: a comedy-heavy cut, a horror-heavy cut, and a toned-down one for TV. He decided the balance of laughs and gore in the editing room.
Brian Robbins, who plays student Steve Williams, grew up to be a director and producer (Varsity Blues, Coach Carter) and is now co-CEO of Paramount Pictures.
Tricia Leigh Fisher (Katie Norton) is the daughter of singer Eddie Fisher and Connie Stevens, and the younger half-sister of Star Wars' Carrie Fisher.
Bill Calvert (Kevin) guest-starred in both China Beach and Quantum Leap in 1988-89, two unrelated shows that each featured a character named Sam Beckett.
Ed Naha wrote the script under the pseudonym M. Kane Jeeves, a name borrowed from W.C. Fields. Naha had also written Honey, I Shrunk the Kids.
Jack Riley, playing Wade Williams, and castmate Michael Bell would later work together again on the animated series Rugrats.
The Williams family's Alaskan wildlife TV special is full of penguins, but penguins live only in the Southern Hemisphere, not Alaska. Nature documentary fail!
Director David Irving is the son of actress Priscilla Pointer and brother of actress Amy Irving, which made Steven Spielberg (Amy's then-husband) his brother-in-law.
Gerrit Graham liked playing Bud so much he adopted the alias Bud T. Chud, and he played a character of that name in David Irving's next film, Night of the Cyclone.
Director David Irving says he has still never seen the original 1984 C.H.U.D., the movie this one is a sequel to.
The script slips in a Smurfs gag. The film also nods to Blazing Saddles, Day of the Dead, Guess Who's Coming to Dinner and Plan 9 from Outer Space.
Per Irving's commentary, studio Vestron struggled to find anyone to direct a script this ambitious with almost no budget.
The poster shows the monsters at a sewer manhole like the first C.H.U.D., but these zombies look different and there are no sewers in the movie at all.
Vestron reportedly figured an underpaid extra could play Bud the Chud cheaply. Director David Irving had to replace an already-cast actor when Gerrit Graham came aboard.
Before directing hits, Brian Robbins (Steve Williams) hosted a late-1980s kids' game show called Pictionary.
Larry Linville, who plays Dr. Jewell, is best known as the pompous Major Frank Burns on M*A*S*H.
IMDb says the film was shot in 1987, two years before its 1989 release, around Southern California including San Pedro, Saugus and East Los Angeles.
June Lockhart, who plays Gracie, was Dr. Maureen Robinson on Lost in Space (1965-68) and Timmy's mom Ruth Martin on Lassie for about 200 episodes.
Gerrit Graham, our Bud, was also in Brian De Palma's Phantom of the Paradise, Used Cars, TerrorVision and Child's Play 2.
Producer Lawrence Kasanoff ran Lightning Pictures, Vestron's genre subsidiary. He later produced the Mortal Kombat movies.
Bud's theme song has music by composer Nicholas Pike, lyrics by Cynthia Garris, and is sung by Kipp Lennon.
Tricia Leigh Fisher once appeared with her mother Connie Stevens and sister Joely Fisher in Bring Me the Head of Dobie Gillis, a 1988 TV reunion movie.
Michael Cudlitz, later a star of The Walking Dead, is credited as a carpenter on this film. He went on to zombie-fighting.
Makeup effects artist Allan Apone says the C.H.U.D. look came from makeup experiments, and the crew made 'C.H.U.D.sicles' using fiberglass molds.
Reviewer Andrew Hatfield on JoBlo called it 'somehow more fun than' the original C.H.U.D. He said it 'isn't scary in the least and that's ok.'
Planned for theaters, this sequel instead came out on VHS and laserdisc from Vestron Video on September 27, 1989.
Rich Hall, who plays Stan, is the comedian who invented Sniglets, the made-up words for things with no name.
Steve's 'Guess who's coming to dinner' quip nods to the 1967 Sidney Poitier film Guess Who's Coming to Dinner, one of several movies this script name-checks.
The movie's tagline was 'This C.H.U.D.'s for you!', a twist on a famous beer slogan. Colonel Masters' line here echoes it.
Bud the C.H.U.D. looks like a comic riff on Bub, the zombie in George Romero's Day of the Dead (1985), which this film references.
Director David Irving said the cast's improvised material made the film hard to assemble in the editing room.
Ritch Shydner, who plays the Mailman, was originally cast as Bud the Chud until Gerrit Graham took the role.
The trick-or-treat gag 'I got a rock' spoofs It's the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown (1966), where Charlie Brown gets a rock in his bag.
Robert Englund, Freddy Krueger himself, has an uncredited cameo as a man in a trench coat walking with the trick-or-treaters.
Robert Englund's cameo as a trench-coated man among the trick-or-treaters was trimmed back by studio Vestron, according to director David Irving's commentary.
Robert Vaughn (Colonel Masters) has a PhD in Communications. His thesis on Hollywood blacklisting was published in 1972 as the book Only Victims.
This is Wall of Voodoo's 'Brave New Dance'. Much of the soundtrack was written and performed by the new wave band's later lineup, with Andy Prieboy on vocals.
Editor Barbara Pokras also cut The Return of the Living Dead, the zombie comedy this film was first conceived as a sequel to.
'I'm a Hungry Man' was written and sung by Andy Prieboy himself, the Wall of Voodoo singer, rather than by the band.
Director David Irving later became chairman of undergraduate film and television at NYU's Tisch School of the Arts. He had earlier directed Rumpelstiltskin.
Director David Irving's mother, actress Priscilla Pointer, plays Dr. Berlin in the film.
Despite her high billing, Bianca Jagger (Mick Jagger's ex-wife) appears only briefly in the film's final scene.
Tricia Leigh Fisher (Katie) says this swimming pool sequence was hard to shoot, and she had to wear a very uncomfortable swimsuit.
Lionsgate put the film on Blu-ray on November 22, 2016, as part of its Vestron Video Collector's Series.
Later films that mention C.H.U.D. II include 28 Days Later (2002), Slither (2006) and Ti West's The House of the Devil (2010).
Gerrit Graham wrote the lyrics to the Grateful Dead song 'Victim or the Crime', set to a tune by Bob Weir.
Robert Vaughn was one of the first actors to play the same character, Napoleon Solo, on three series: The Man from U.N.C.L.E., Please Don't Eat the Daisies and The Girl from U.N.C.L.E.
